# Package layout

`aussiefy/` is one flat package whose modules fall into layers. Each layer may use the layers below it, never
the ones above. The layering is documented here and enforced by `tests/architecture/test_layers.py`, rather than by
subpackages (see [DD-006](decisions/dd-006-layered-flat-package.md)).

| Layer | Modules |
|---|---|
| Public API | `__init__.py` (translate, lookup, lint, guide, plan, yarn, Translator, load_dictionary, verify, and the result and error types) |
| Surfaces (thin adapters) | `cli.py`, `mcp_server.py`, `skills/aussiefy/SKILL.md` |
| Toolkit | `harness.py` (gathers lookup, lint and guide, and adds `plan` and `translate`), `lookup.py`, `lint.py`, `guide.py`, `verify.py` (fidelity and policy checks), `align.py` (shared sentence counterparts) |
| Document translation | `translation.py` (shared surface routing), `markdown.py` (strict source spans and document results), `markup.py` (extended Markdown/MDX scanning) |
| LLM modes | `yarn.py` (yarn mode), `llm.py` (surface and sentence rewrites), `claude.py` (the one Claude client) |
| Engine | `engine.py` (the pipeline), `text.py`, `matcher.py`, `detect.py`, `select.py`, `realise.py`, `morph.py`, `garnish.py`, `context.py`, `policy.py`, `genre.py` (pure form policy and classification), `dialect.py` (source-English swaps), `pos.py` (bundled tagger), `protected.py` (opaque source spans and restoration) |
| Dictionary | `schema.py` (entries, concepts), `model.py` (the dictionary as data, and what derives from it), `loader.py` (reading and validating the YAML), `terms.py` (when two spellings are one term), `dump.py` |
| Similarity | `embed.py`, `static.py` (the bundled model), `models.py` (installed ones) |
| Maintainers | `gaps.py`, `explain.py`, `rounds.py` (research rounds), `judge.py` (blind packets, report validation and optional Claude boundary), `scrape/` (scrape, fragments, harvest, tag, review) |
| Shared | `errors.py` (`UserError`, the error a user can fix) |

The data the engine reads is in `aussiefy/data/` (see [the dictionary](../functional/dictionary.md)).

## The layering rule

The core (the engine, the dictionary and the similarity modules other than `models.py`) imports nothing from
the toolkit, the LLM modes, the surfaces or the maintainer tools, so it stays usable and testable on its own.
`tests/architecture/test_layers.py` checks this with an import scan, and allows one exception: `embed.make_embedder("local")`
resolves the installed model's settings through `models.py`, the one place the core reaches out. A second test
keeps the dictionary model (`model.py`, `schema.py`, `policy.py`, `matcher.py`, `text.py`, `genre.py`) free of the loader's
file I/O.

Crikey, Optional heavy dependencies \(anthropic, mcp, sentence\-transformers, torch\) are imported lazily, inside the
functions that need them, so the core imports'n runs with its core dependencies, offline. Markdown's light parser
heaps only in that mode; the plain engine never imports its adapter \([DD-015](decisions/dd-015-source-preserving-markdown.md)).

## Where to change things

- New slang, a new concept or a different level behaviour: the data in `aussiefy/data/`, Stone the flamin' crows, not the code.
- A new way of detectin' or realisin' a meaning: the engine stage that owns it \([pipeline](pipeline.md)).
- A new agent-facing operation or parameter: the toolkit function first, then each surface, which
  `tests/functional/test_interfaces.py` holds in step.
- Anything that talks to Claude: through `claude.py`, the single seam for the SDK.

Stone the crows, Genre configuration'n the POS vocabulary are loaded once into the selected dictionary. Anyway, the classifier and
model derive values without opening files. Well, Syntax scanners supply opaque source spans to the engine; no bloody way
Markdown/JSX rules enter its core. See [DD-016](decisions/dd-016-reconcile-source-capabilities.md).
